items.text:
मुक्तिमिच्छासि चेत्तात ! विषयान् विषवत्त्यज ।
क्षमाऽऽर्जवं दया शौचं सत्यं पीयूषवत्पिब ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
muktimicchāsi cettāta ! viṣayān viṣavattyaja |
kṣamā''rjavaṃ dayā śaucaṃ satyaṃ pīyūṣavatpiba || 1 ||
items.en: My child, if you want freedom, give up the pleasures of the senses as if they were poison, and drink in forgiveness, honesty, kindness, purity and truth as if they were nectar.

items.text:
परस्परस्य मर्माणि ये भाषन्ते नराधमाः ।
त एव विलयं यान्ति वल्मीकोदरसर्पवत् ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
parasparasya marmāṇi ye bhāṣante narādhamāḥ |
ta eva vilayaṃ yānti valmīkodarasarpavat || 2 ||
items.en: Low people who reveal each other's secret weak points destroy themselves, like a snake trapped inside an anthill.

items.text:
गन्धः सुवर्णे फलभिक्षुदंडे-
नाऽकारि पुष्पं खलु चन्दनस्य ।
विद्वान् धनी भूपतिदीर्घजीवी
धातुः पुरा कोऽपि न बुध्दिदोऽभूत् ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
gandhaḥ suvarṇe phalabhikṣudaṃḍe-
nā'kāri puṣpaṃ khalu candanasya |
vidvān dhanī bhūpatidīrghajīvī
dhātuḥ purā ko'pi na budhdido'bhūt || 3 ||
items.en: The Creator gave no scent to gold, no fruit to sugarcane, no flowers to sandalwood; he did not make the learned rich or kings long-lived. It seems no one was there to advise him.

items.text:
सर्वौषधीनाममृतं प्रधानम्
सर्वेषु सौख्येष्वशनं प्रधानम् ।
सर्वेन्द्रियाणां नयनं प्रधानं
सर्वेषु गात्रेषु शिरः प्रधानम्।
॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
sarvauṣadhīnāmamṛtaṃ pradhānam
sarveṣu saukhyeṣvaśanaṃ pradhānam |
sarvendriyāṇāṃ nayanaṃ pradhānaṃ
sarveṣu gātreṣu śiraḥ pradhānam|
|| 4 ||
items.en: Nectar is the chief of all medicines, food is the chief of all comforts, the eye is the chief of all senses, and the head is the chief of all parts of the body.

items.text:
दुतो न सञ्चरति खे न चलेच्च वार्ता ।
पुर्व न जल्पितमिदं न च सड्गमोऽस्ति ।
व्योम्नि स्थितं रविशाशग्रहणं प्रशस्तं
जानाति यो द्विजवरः सकथं न विद्वान् ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
duto na sañcarati khe na calecca vārtā |
purva na jalpitamidaṃ na ca saḍgamo'sti |
vyomni sthitaṃ raviśāśagrahaṇaṃ praśastaṃ
jānāti yo dvijavaraḥ sakathaṃ na vidvān || 5 ||
items.en: No messenger travels through the sky, no news comes from there, no one said it before, and no one has gone there; yet the Brahmin who can tell when the sun and moon will be eclipsed, how is he not learned?

items.text:
विद्यार्थी सेवकः पान्थः क्षुधार्तो भयकातरः ।
भाण्डारी प्रतिहारी च सप्त सुप्तान् प्रबोधयेत् ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
vidyārthī sevakaḥ pānthaḥ kṣudhārto bhayakātaraḥ |
bhāṇḍārī pratihārī ca sapta suptān prabodhayet || 6 ||
items.en: Wake these seven if they are sleeping: a student, a servant, a traveller, a hungry person, a frightened person, a storekeeper and a gatekeeper.

items.text:
अहिं नृपं च शार्दुलं बरटि बालकं तथा ।
परश्वानं च मूर्ख च सप्त सुप्तान्न बोधयेत् ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
ahiṃ nṛpaṃ ca śārdulaṃ baraṭi bālakaṃ tathā |
paraśvānaṃ ca mūrkha ca sapta suptānna bodhayet || 7 ||
items.en: Do not wake these seven if they are sleeping: a snake, a king, a tiger, a wasp, a small child, someone else's dog and a fool.

items.text:
अर्थाधीताश्चयै र्वेदास्तथा शूद्रान्न भोजिनः ।
ते द्विजाः किं करिष्यन्ति निर्विषा इव पन्नगाः ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
arthādhītāścayai rvedāstathā śūdrānna bhojinaḥ |
te dvijāḥ kiṃ kariṣyanti nirviṣā iva pannagāḥ || 8 ||
items.en: Brahmins who study the Vedas for money and live on the food of low people, what can they do? They are like snakes without poison.

items.text:
यस्मिन रुष्टे भयं नास्ति तुष्टे नैव धनागमः ।
निग्रहाऽनुग्रहोनास्ति स रुष्टः किं करिष्यति ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
yasmina ruṣṭe bhayaṃ nāsti tuṣṭe naiva dhanāgamaḥ |
nigrahā'nugrahonāsti sa ruṣṭaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati || 9 ||
items.en: If a person's anger causes no fear and his pleasure brings no reward, if he can neither punish nor help, what can his anger do?

items.text:
निविषेणापि सर्पेण कर्तव्या महती फणा ।
विषमस्तु न चाप्यस्तु घटाटोप भयंकरः ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
niviṣeṇāpi sarpeṇa kartavyā mahatī phaṇā |
viṣamastu na cāpyastu ghaṭāṭopa bhayaṃkaraḥ || 10 ||
items.en: Even a snake with no poison should raise a big hood; whether there is poison or not, the show alone frightens.

items.text:
प्रारर्द्यूतप्रसंगेन मध्यान्हे स्त्रीप्रसंगतः ।
रात्रौ चौरप्रसंगेन कालो गच्छति धीमताम् ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
prārardyūtaprasaṃgena madhyānhe strīprasaṃgataḥ |
rātrau cauraprasaṃgena kālo gacchati dhīmatām || 11 ||
items.en: The wise pass their time in the morning with a story about gambling, at midday with a story about a woman, and at night with a story about a thief.

items.text:
स्वहस्तग्रथिता माला स्वहस्ताद घृष्टचन्दनम् ।
स्वहस्तलिखितं शक्रस्यापि श्रियं हरेत् ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
svahastagrathitā mālā svahastāda ghṛṣṭacandanam |
svahastalikhitaṃ śakrasyāpi śriyaṃ haret || 12 ||
items.en: A garland strung with one's own hands, sandal paste ground with one's own hands, and a text written with one's own hands would take away the glory even of Indra.

items.text:
इक्षुदंडास्तिलाः शुद्राः कान्ता कांचनमोदिनी ।
चन्दनं दधि ताम्बूलं मर्दनं गुणवर्ध्दनम् ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
ikṣudaṃḍāstilāḥ śudrāḥ kāntā kāṃcanamodinī |
candanaṃ dadhi tāmbūlaṃ mardanaṃ guṇavardhdanam || 13 ||
items.en: Sugarcane, sesame, a lowly person, a woman, gold, earth, sandalwood, curd and betel leaf: these improve when they are pressed or rubbed.

items.text:
दरिद्रता धीरतया विराजते ।
कुवस्त्रता शुभ्रतया विराजते ॥
कदन्नता चोष्णतया विराजते ।
कुरूपता शीलतया विराजते ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr:
daridratā dhīratayā virājate |
kuvastratā śubhratayā virājate ||
kadannatā coṣṇatayā virājate |
kurūpatā śīlatayā virājate || 14 ||
items.en: Poverty is made bright by courage, old clothes by keeping them clean, poor food by serving it hot, and plain looks by good character.
